newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung denies signing deal with Fokker.
newsitem.headline: Samsung denies signing deal with Fokker.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries denied on Tuesday news reports that it had signed a letter of intent to take over bankrupt planemaker Fokker NV.
"We have conveyed our intention to take over Fokker but it's not true we signed a letter of intent," spokesman Park Jong Hyon said. "We are still holding talks with the company."
The Financial Times reported on Tuesday morning that the rescue of Fokker grew more likely on Monday when Samsung Aerospace Industries said it had issued a letter of intent.
Fokker officials refused to confirm the reports.
The receivers of the bankrupt Dutch planemaker said last week that Samsung was carrying out an exclusive due diligence at the Dutch firm.
Samsung Aerospace, a unit of the Samsung Group, had carried out takeover talks on two earlier occasions, one prior to Fokkers's collpase and one immediately after it.
Park also denied a report by Dutch daily de Volkskrant that the takeover price "will not be far away from" $130-150 million.
"It's too early to guess it," he said. "All we can say now is we are still interested in Fokker as we did before."
He also declined comment on local news reports that Samsung Aerospace would form a consortium for the deal.
